taxonomic_note: Accepted by current Kew/POWO. Two accepted varieties are recognized: var. linearifolia and var. arenicola. The Central Texas Edwards Plateau learner stays species-level unless a specimen/photo set provides diagnostic varietal evidence.
look_here_first: Start with the life cycle and leaves. Tetraneuris linearifolia is the annual Tetraneuris: slender stems with narrow linear to narrowly oblanceolate leaves, often hairy and gland-dotted. Then confirm the solitary yellow heads, hairy multi-series phyllaries, and the characteristic four-to-eight scale-like pappus structures.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Travis — UT Plant Resources Center Travis County Asteraceae herbarium index includes Tetraneuris linearifolia var. linearifolia. San Saba — Bierner & Turner 2003 cite an exact San Saba County specimen. Kerr — Kerr Wildlife Management Area vascular-flora checklist documents Tetraneuris linearifolia with voucher collections.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: Species-level PASS only. Joey's Edwards Plateau frames are not used to infer var. linearifolia versus var. arenicola; variety assignment requires diagnostic evidence.

best_field_traits: leaves alternate, simple, very narrow linear to narrowly oblanceolate/spatulate
solitary radiate yellow heads on long slender peduncles
involucre with multiple series of distinct phyllaries
ray florets yellow and typically 3-lobed at the tips
cypselae with a persistent pappus of several scale-like units
morphology_keys.family_training: Use this species as an Asteraceae comparison where vegetative characters matter before the head is dissected: linear foliage and woolly/hairy texture are strong field cues, but final confirmation comes from capitulum, phyllaries, ray/disc florets and cypsela/pappus.
morphology_keys.video_training: Use the Edwards Plateau frames for whole-plant habit and woolly linear foliage, then the Southern Texas frame for the underside of the capitulum and phyllary architecture.

comparisons.key_distinctions: T. linearifolia is annual; the other common local Tetraneuris comparison species are perennial. In the field, combine life cycle/base architecture with narrow foliage, pubescence, head structure and pappus rather than relying on flower color.
